failureMessage: waitForFunction takes an async predicate's promise as truthy and resolves at once, on every engine, so the test passes only while the page happens to be fast
fix: wait with until(page, fn, arg) from web-tests/page_until.mjs, which polls the page until the async predicate resolves truthy

matchLines.what: waits on an async predicate with waitForFunction, which never waits: {match}

failureMessage: a test that sleeps a fixed time guesses how long the page takes: too short on a slow runner, so it flakes, and wasted on every fast one
fix: wait for what the next check reads, hold a stand-in's answer with held(), or move ctx.clock; else end the line `// waits on purpose: <reason>`, or `// bounds a hang: <reason>`

matchLines.what: waits a fixed time instead of for what it needs: {match}

failureMessage: a frame wait copied into each driver drifts: one waits one frame, the next two, and nobody can say which a page needs
fix: import frames(page, n) from web-tests/page_frames.mjs; where a wait in the page itself is needed, end the line `// waits on purpose: <reason>`

failureMessage: Google is a detail of the remote store and the identity provider, so code elsewhere that depends on it breaks when that detail changes
fix: move it into web/drive.js (behind `remote`) or web/account.js; an older browser key or cache path may stay, as a constant alone on its line

matchLines.what: names Google or Drive outside web/drive.js and web/account.js: {match}

failureMessage: a timer set anywhere in page code is a cadence nobody can list, a visual effect guessing how long it takes, or a poll running on in a hidden tab
fix: make a visual effect a CSS motion that animations off keeps running where needed, background work every(), settle(), within() or after() from web/pacing.js; else end the line `// timed here: <reason>`

failureMessage: the browser keeps every value page code hands the console, its last thousand messages for the page's life: a logged error keeps its stack, a logged result its data
fix: log through warn() or note() from web/log.js, which hands the console text alone

matchLines.what: writes to the console outside web/log.js: {match}

failureMessage: a study's literature folder holds only Markdown; a PDF, a figure, a crop or supplementary code copies the publisher's material into a public repository
fix: fold what the file says into the paper's studies/<study>/docs/literature/<slug>.md, link the original at its publisher (DOI, supplementary URL), and delete the file; the paper-intake skill says how

checkEachFile.what: is not Markdown, in the literature folder
checkEachFile.fix: fold it into the paper's <slug>.md as text and links, then delete it

failureMessage: the page's animations-off setting stops every CSS transition and animation, so code waiting on one's end never runs: a popup stays open, a class is never cleared
fix: keep the motion ending under :root[data-motion="off"] in web/style.css, or show it never starts then; test it so, and end the line `// ends with animations off: <how>`

matchLines.what: acts on a CSS motion's end, which animations off never fires: {match}

failureMessage: Python belongs to the studies, the lab, the page tests' fixtures and the dev tools; elsewhere it is a second language in a part of the repo that is JavaScript
fix: write it in JavaScript, or move it into the study, test or build tool it serves

checkEachFile.what: is Python outside the folders Python is allowed in

failureMessage: the page reaches a study's Python only through the worker's ready() and Session.call(action, args); page code that starts or drives Pyodide itself is a second way in
fix: add the action to the study's Session.call and ask for it through the worker

matchLines.what: starts or drives Python outside the worker: {match}

failureMessage: a test that reads a study's downloaded images fails or skips wherever they were not fetched, so CI never exercises it, and no test downloads real data
fix: draw a small image in the test (studies/nor/tests/synthetic_nor.py draws NoR's) instead of reading the study's data/raw folder
